prompt.context: Your client is BevCo, a global company that sells a wide variety of non-alcoholic beverages. Their operations are predominantly in North America. BevCo sells primarily to retailers, restaurants, bars and wholesalers. Recently, competition has been rising, giving consumers more choices over brand as well as type of beverage. This, in turn, has put pressure on margins. BevCo has hired us to make recommendations on what actions to take. BevCo is involved in the production and marketing of beverage drinks. They do not distribute. Segments of drinks include: Sugar (carbonated drinks, e.g. Coke, Fanta), Juice, Water, Tea/Coffee, Sports (e.g. Gatorade), Energy (e.g. Red Bull), Diet. Some segments, like Energy, have grown considerably in recent years. There are a few other large industry players.
prompt.question: BevCo has hired us to make recommendations on what actions to take given rising competition and margin pressure. What would you recommend?

clarifying_info.q: Does BevCo handle its own distribution?
What geographies does BevCo operate in?
clarifying_info.a: Operations are predominantly in North America.
BevCo sells primarily to retailers, restaurants, bars, and wholesalers.

exhibits.title: BevCo Sales by Segment
exhibits.shows: A chart showing BevCo's sales last year (in $millions) by segment alongside each segment's year-over-year sales growth rate.

framework: Understand current portfolio: segment-level sales, growth trends, and profitability
Diagnose root cause of margin pressure: volume loss in large segments vs. gains in small/fast-growing segments
Assess consumer demand shifts driving segment dynamics (health, demographics, trends)
Size the opportunity in high-growth segments (e.g., Energy drinks) to evaluate strategic pivot
Develop recommendations: defend/harvest cash-cow segments vs. invest in growth segments
Identify risks and next steps for execution

questions.prompt: Interpret Exhibit A: What is the overall situation for BevCo based on the sales data?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that BevCo's largest segments (Sugar and Juice) are declining while smaller segments (Energy, Sports, Water) are growing. Key hypothesis: BevCo may be over-indexing on fast-growing but small segments at the expense of its largest revenue sources. Total revenue is falling despite growth in new segments because the absolute dollar losses in Sugar and Juice outweigh gains elsewhere.

math.setup: Compute total sales last year, total sales this year, and overall growth using segment data from Exhibit A.
math.answer: Total sales last year: $100M; total sales this year: $93M; overall growth: -7%

questions.prompt: What are the consumer drivers behind the shift in industry dynamics (i.e., why are Water, Sports, and Energy growing while Sugar and Juice are declining)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm demand-side factors. Strong answers include: (1) Health consciousness — consumers shifting away from sugary drinks toward water, sports drinks, and perceived-functional beverages; (2) Demographics — growing proportion of young people who are more health-aware, sporty, and trend-driven; (3) Trendiness / social signaling — energy and sports drinks carry lifestyle associations (e.g., Red Bull, Gatorade); (4) Sports participation — increasing recreational and competitive sports activity driving sports drink demand; (5) Diet preferences — though Diet is also declining, broader low-sugar trend benefits Water and light beverages.

questions.prompt: BevCo wants to assess the opportunity of the Energy Drinks market in the US, specifically targeting young males aged 16-32. How large is this opportunity in terms of revenue and profit?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize this as a market-sizing exercise. Before calculating, the candidate should identify the key components: (1) size of target population, (2) consumption habits of that population, (3) BevCo's achievable market share, price, and margin. A strong candidate lays out the approach before crunching numbers and flags that the result should be compared to current segment sizes for context.

math.setup: Estimate annual revenue and profit for BevCo from targeting 16-32 year-old males in the US Energy Drinks market. Assumptions provided: US population = 300M, half male, life expectancy = 80 years, uniform age distribution, target age group drinks ~20 energy drinks/year, BevCo market share = 5%, price = $3/drink, gross margin = 20%.
steps: Target population: 300M x 50% (male) x (16/80) (age fraction 16-32 = 16 years out of 80) = 300M x 0.5 x 0.2 = 30 million males aged 16-32
Total market drinks/year: 30M x 20 drinks = 600 million drinks
BevCo volume: 600M x 5% market share = 30 million drinks
BevCo profit: $90M x 20% gross margin = $18 million
math.answer: BevCo potential revenue: $90M/year; potential gross profit: $18M/year. Note: $90M would be larger than BevCo's current largest segment (Sugar at ~$39M this year), indicating a very significant opportunity.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the consumer drivers behind the shift in industry dynamics — why are some segments growing while others are declining?

categories.name: Health & Wellness
ideas: Consumers are more health-conscious and reducing sugar intake
Shift toward functional beverages perceived as healthier (water, sports drinks)
Diet concerns driving away from sugar-heavy carbonated drinks

categories.name: Demographics
ideas: Growing proportion of younger consumers (Millennials, Gen Z) who have different preferences
Younger cohorts are more active and sports-oriented
Younger consumers more influenced by lifestyle branding

categories.name: Trendiness & Lifestyle
ideas: Energy and sports drinks carry aspirational lifestyle associations
Social media amplifies trends around beverages
Celebrity and athlete endorsements boosting Energy and Sports segments

categories.name: Sports & Activity
ideas: Increased recreational and competitive sports participation drives Sports drink demand
Workplace wellness programs encouraging active lifestyles
Energy drinks appeal to gaming, late-night work, and performance culture

categories.name: Product Innovation
ideas: New flavors and functional ingredients in Energy and Sports segments attract trial
Traditional Sugar and Juice segments see less innovation
Water segment benefits from premium/sparkling/flavored water innovation

recommendation: BevCo should not abandon its core Sugar and Juice segments, which still represent the largest share of revenue; it must stabilize and defend these through pricing, marketing, or product reformulation

BevCo should invest meaningfully in the Energy and Sports drink segments, where consumer demand trends are strong and the market opportunity is substantial (up to $90M in Energy alone for the target demographic)
A portfolio rebalancing approach is warranted: harvest mature segments efficiently while allocating growth capital to high-trajectory segments
risks: Rapid decline in Juice (-50% YoY) may signal structural shift rather than cyclical — needs further diagnosis before committing resources
Energy market is highly competitive with established players (Red Bull, Monster); capturing 5% market share may require significant brand-building investment
Neglecting core segments while pivoting to growth segments could accelerate revenue decline if execution is slow
Margin profile of new segments (Energy, Sports) may differ from established segments — need full P&L analysis, not just gross margin
recommendation.risks_note: Candidates should flag these as areas for further due diligence.
next_steps: Conduct deep-dive profitability analysis by segment (gross margin, contribution margin) to confirm which segments are actually profitable
Assess competitive positioning in Energy and Sports vs. established players
Determine whether Juice decline is structural (consumer shift) or tactical (pricing, distribution issue)
Develop go-to-market plan for Energy segment targeting 16-32 male demographic
Evaluate whether brand/product investment or M&A is the faster path to gaining share in high-growth segments
